metadata.audit_scope_note: Benchmark-matched network (Arabidopsis PSoup ortholog crosswalk via networks/Tillering_Sorghum_Benchmark/data/ortholog_crosswalk.json). Gap audit prioritized around the crosswalk's own 18-gene set, not the broader rice tillering gene set covered by the sister network networks/Tillering_Sorghum (MOC1/MOC3/LAX1/LAX2/FON1/DEP1/SD1/NGR5/OsMADS23/OsBZR1 intentionally out of scope here).

residual_gaps_for_builder.description: GT1->NCED3 (E020) rests on DOI 10.1007/s12374-021-09310-9 (Song et al., OsGT1/HOX12 downstream of FC1), which was already tried and quarantined for this exact claim in the sister Tillering_Sorghum network (evidence.json: 'no paper found within budget that co-mentions GT1 and NCED1'). Targeted WebSearch in this pass found no dedicated GT1-ABA/NCED mechanistic paper in rice or sorghum. BUILDER/Step 1.6 should expect this edge to quarantine again; treat GT1->NCED3 as a literature_gap-flavoured link (biologically plausible ABA crosstalk downstream of the BRC1/GT1 axis, but not yet directly evidenced) unless Step 1.6 finds a co-mention.

FHY3FAR1 (E039-E042, T016) remains Arabidopsis-only evidence (10.1038/s41467-020-15893-7). Targeted search for a rice/sorghum/maize-specific FHY3/FAR1-tillering or FHY3/FAR1-strigolactone paper found none accessible this pass (maize FHY3/FAR1 literature is drought-context only, not branching). Crosswalk correctly keeps this flagged 'unconfirmed' - unclosable with current search budget.

CLAMT crosswalk gap only partially closed: Os4OCLAMT (Kayoumu et al. 2024, Science Advances, 10.1126/sciadv.adq3942) is a real named rice CLAMT-class enzyme, but it acts on the noncanonical 4-oxo-CLA branch, not the canonical CLA branch the network's MAX1->CLAMT->LBO edges model, and its mutant (oscyp706c2) shows no tillering phenotype. Documented in ortholog_crosswalk.json only; no curated_edges/perturbation_dataset entry was added on this DOI since it would not directly support the existing E013/E014 claims. MAX1->CLAMT (E013) and CLAMT->LBO (E014) remain on their original DOIs (Yoda 2021 sorghum-direct for MAX1, Arabidopsis pcp.pcad060 for CLAMT->LBO respectively).

edges_added: E043 (MAX4->MAX1, sign +1, DOI 10.1111/nph.17737 - Yoda et al. 2021 New Phytologist, sorghum-direct: SbMAX1a-d act on carlactone produced by the D27->CCD7(MAX3)->CCD8(MAX4) branch; closes the previously-orphaned MAX1 in-degree=0 gap by linking two genes already in the node set)
tests_added: T028 (CXE overexpression, up, Zea mays, DOI 10.3389/fpls.2021.639401 - Roesler et al. 2021 Frontiers: ectopic AtCXE20 in maize increases branches/tillers; gives the CXE node its first grass-species functional test, previously Arabidopsis-only via T014)

T029 (Gibberellin treatment_high, dn, Oryza sativa, DOI 10.1038/s41467-019-10667-2 - same verified DOI already grounding E037; closes missing-treatment-test gap for the GA hormone node, consistent with the existing Gibberellin->Tiller_Number(-1) edge)

T030 (Decapitation_Signal / decapitation, up, Oryza sativa, DOI 10.3390/plants13010091 - Chen et al. 2024 Plants MDPI, rice decapitation-vs-strigolactone proteomics study; closes missing canonical-decapitation-mutant gap for a PSoup-benchmark-central perturbation type that had no direct test despite Decapitation_Signal having 2 downstream edges)
crosswalk_updates: CLAMT (unconfirmed -> Os4OCLAMT, Oryza sativa, medium confidence, documentation-only)
CXE (unconfirmed -> AtCXE20 ectopic in Zea mays, medium confidence, closed via T028)
